title: A growable byte buffer — bin_builder
text: bin_builder() creates buffer bytes appended bin_put() taken bin_take(). grows doubling (half past 64 MiB), million appends cost dozen reallocations, million copies; never grows past max.

title: A growable byte buffer — bin_builder

title: A growable byte buffer — bin_builder
text: builder external pointer: copied modification, every function changes place, survive saveRDS() restored session; using restored builder zubin_invalid_argument error. memory freed garbage collected. bin_take(b) returns bytes empties builder, keeps capacity accepts new appends; .raw(b) returns copy leaves builder . bin_reserve(b, n) makes room n bytes now, bin_reset(b) empties builder without freeing storage, bin_size(b) number bytes holds.

title: Describe a binary record — bin_layout
Describe a binary record — bin_layout
text: spec specification string; named character vector type tokens, whose names field names (c(id = "u32", "x3")); zubin_layout, returned unchanged. endian byte order fields specification order : "little", "big", "native", host's (see bin_info()). align FALSE packed fields, TRUE C struct alignment.

title: Describe a binary record — bin_layout
text: zubin_layout: list spec, normalised specification; fields, data frame columns name, type, count (array elements, 1 scalar), size, offset endian (NA one-byte types); size, record size bytes; align, record's alignment (1 packed). length() names() describe fields carry values, excludes padding; .data.frame() returns fields; bin_size() returns size.

title: Describe a binary record — bin_layout
text: One string fields separated whitespace comma:   example "<magic:u32 version:u16 flags:u16 count:u64 name:s32", "<ts:i64 price:f64 qty:i32 side:u8 x3 crc:u32.". endian prefix overrides endian, field's .le .suffix overrides . Names unique; unnamed field called V1, V2, ... position among fields padding. t[k] array k elements, numeric types bool (write b24, b8[3]). Every malformed specification zubin_spec_error carrying position, 0-based byte position problem string.
code: layout  := [ endian ] field { sep field } endian  := "<" | ">" | "="          little, big, host; default `endian` field   := [ name ":" ] type [ "[" count "]" ] [ "." order ]          | "x" width                padding: never read, written as zeros type    := u8 i8 u16 i16 u32 i32 u64 i64 f16 bf16 f32 f64 bool          | "b" width                fixed bytes          | "s" width                fixed string order   := "le" | "be"              multi-byte numeric types only name    := [A-Za-z_] [A-Za-z0-9_.]* count, width := 1 .. 2^31 - 1

title: Describe a binary record — bin_layout
text: align = FALSE fields packed consecutive offsets. align = TRUE field starts next multiple element width (1 bool, b, s x) record size rounded largest : rule C compilers apply struct 64-bit targets, struct written fwrite() reads back align = TRUE. (32-bit x86 aligns 8-byte members 4 inside struct; struct needs explicit x padding.)

title: Describe a binary record — bin_layout
code: wav <- bin_layout("<riff:s4 size:u32 wave:s4") wav #> <zubin_layout: 12 bytes, 3 fields> #>  name type count size offset endian #>  riff s4   1     4    0             #>  size u32  1     4    4      little #>  wave s4   1     4    8             bin_size(wav) #> [1] 12 wav$fields #>   name type count size offset endian #> 1 riff   s4     1    4      0   <NA> #> 2 size  u32     1    4      4 little #> 3 wave   s4     1    4      8   <NA>  # The same, built programmatically bin_layout(c(riff = "s4", size = "u32", wave = "s4")) #> <zubin_layout: 12 bytes, 3 fields> #>  name type count size offset endian #>  riff s4   1     4    0             #>  size u32  1     4    4      little #>  wave s4   1     4    8              # A C struct { uint8_t a; uint32_t b; uint16_t c; } bin_layout("a:u8 b:u32 c:u16", endian = "native", align = TRUE)$fields #>   name type count size offset endian #> 1    a   u8     1    1      0   <NA> #> 2    b  u32     1    4      4 little #> 3    c  u16     1    2      8 little
